doc.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: The banjo band at My Father's Moustache and learning endurance
summary: The Dixieland band had two banjos and washboard; six-hour nights taught him pacing and relaxation.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: In the Your Father’s Moustache band, was that sort of a typical banjo?

Plectrum and tenor — loud as hell. Lord have mercy, loud as hell. And they had a microphone and they were singing, and they had a trombone player that was even louder than that and a guy named Joe Terra who dressed up in a clown’s outfit playing washboard. He was really good [scats]. He swung, actually. I mean he was killing. And they even had another guy that worked for NBC sports and he would play washboard with laying it on his lap but he would do it with knives. [scats] I mean these guys really did swing actually, they were great. And that’s what I would do Friday night and Saturday night from 8:30 to 3:30 in the morning.

Do you understand? And a swollen lip later. Cuts, you know what I mean? They all had microphones and I was blowing a bossa nova all night long. So like I said that’s the gig I cut my teeth on so everything after that was a piece of cake. I never complained about a two or three hour gig after — so what, it ain’t nothing. I used to work six hours.

You know what I mean? Really. But the gig actually taught me how, people get amazed with my endurance now when I’m playing, standing up there playing tuba bass for an hour at a time, and they say like, “How do you do that?” I mean that’s how I did it because I learned doing six hours. And I learned how to pace myself, I learned how to blow and relax. Because what kills you when you don’t relax. If you don’t relax you’ll get tired. The tension, you’ll get tired, when you get tired you slow down, you slow down the whole process you know, because you’re finished. So I had to learn how to relax and do that job.
